key_insight: AVGen-Bench introduces a task-driven, multi-granular benchmark that evaluates text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation jointly across audio, visual, and temporal dimensions—capturing fine-grained correctness and synchronization that prior, embedding-based or isolated benchmarks miss.
problem_solved: Addresses fragmented T2AV evaluation by providing a standardized suite of high-quality prompts and multi-level metrics to measure joint alignment, fidelity, and synchronization for realistic prompts across 11 real-world categories.
method: Curate a diverse set of high-quality, task-driven prompts spanning 11 real-world categories to stress different T2AV capabilities.

Define a multi-granular evaluation protocol combining automated metrics (e.g., audio fidelity, visual fidelity, cross-modal alignment, temporal synchronization) with targeted human judgments and per-task correctness checks.
Provide standardized benchmarking procedures, reference sets, and score aggregation so different models can be compared consistently on joint audio–video performance.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably compare and improve T2AV systems using fine-grained, task-aware metrics—accelerating development of models that produce coherent, synchronized audio and video from text prompts.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: prompt → model → audio+video outputs → multi-granular metric computation (segment, event, scene levels).
Heatmap or radar chart comparing models across metric axes (alignment, audio fidelity, visual fidelity, sync) and categories.
Side-by-side examples: prompt, generated short video frames + waveform, and a compact scorecard showing per-metric scores.
Bar chart or leaderboard showing aggregated benchmark scores across the 11 real-world categories.
paper_title: AVGen-Bench: A Task-Driven Benchmark for Multi-Granular Evaluation of Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
paper_authors: Ziwei Zhou, Zeyuan Lai, Rui Wang, Yifan Yang, Zhen Xing
